title: Keep partial output and inspect every pipeline stage
goal: Use tee and immediate PIPESTATUS to distinguish useful partial output from a successful pipeline.
challenge: Retain the supplied producer’s partial output in a file and downstream result. Show all stage statuses, then demonstrate pipefail and distinguish grep no-match from an input error.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/textarchive-tee.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/textarchive-tee.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command:
here && fresh capture.txt sorted.txt stages.txt && { bash -c 'printf "beta
alpha
"; exit 7' | tee capture.txt | LC_ALL=C sort > sorted.txt; ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"); printf '%s
' "${ps[*]}" > stages.txt; test "${ps[*]}" = '7 0 0'; } && cat stages.txt sorted.txt
steps.explanation: Even an assignment or echo changes PIPESTATUS: snapshot it immediately. The last stage succeeding does not erase upstream failure or partial files.
steps.expected: 7 0 0; sorted alpha/beta and retained unsorted producer bytes.

steps.command: here && fresh pipefail.txt && { bash -o pipefail -c 'printf "partial\n"; exit 7' | cat > pipefail.txt; ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"); test "${ps[*]}" = '7 0'; }
steps.explanation: The child’s pipefail setting alone does not change the parent pipeline policy. Stage statuses still establish failure.
steps.expected: The file retains partial; upstream7, downstream0.

steps.command: here && fresh policy.txt codes.txt && { bash -o pipefail -c 'bash -c '\''printf "partial\n"; exit 7'\'' | tee policy.txt >/dev/null'; rc=$?; grep -F absent capture.txt >/dev/null; nomatch=$?; grep -F absent missing.txt >/dev/null 2>&1; error=$?; printf '%s %s %s\n' "$rc" "$nomatch" "$error" > codes.txt; test "$rc $nomatch $error" = '7 1 2'; } && cat codes.txt
steps.explanation: Enable pipefail in the shell which owns the pipeline. grep status1 means no selected line, not status2 input failure.
steps.expected: 7 1 2, with the actual partial file retained.

hints: Snapshot the whole array before any diagnostic command.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
